vintage: Small Business Pulse Survey Phase 8, week 72, collected April 11 to 17, 2022 (the last week the cash-on-hand question was asked)
title: Small Business Pulse Survey: How would you describe the current availability of cash on hand for this business?
universe: Nonfarm, single-location employer businesses with 1 to 499 employees and receipts of $1,000 or more in the 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico
questionnaireQuote: Q12. How would you describe the current availability of cash on hand for this business, including any financial assistance or loans? Currently, cash on hand will cover: 1-7 days of business operations; 1-2 weeks of business operations; 3-4 weeks of business operations; 1-2 months of business operations; 3 or more months of business operations; No cash available for business operations; Don't know
limits: Experimental, nonprobability weekly panel. Self-reported months of operations covered, counting pandemic financial assistance and loans, in April 2022 after the Paycheck Protection Program, Economic Injury Disaster Loans and the Restaurant Revitalization Fund, so the upper buckets are inflated against a normal year (Accommodation and Food Services, the lowest-cash industry in the JPMorgan Chase Institute sample, reports 31.5 percent at 3 or more months here, above the 30.6 percent of all sectors). Buckets are coarse, 3 or more months is open-ended and there is no bucket between 2 and 3 months. Used only as an independent cross-check of the lower tail (no cash, 1 to 7 days) and of the direction of the upper tail; it sets no parameter value. Island areas other than Puerto Rico are outside the survey.
